candidate.answerReason: Positive-area partial overlap places the triangles on the same side of their common hypotenuse with their acute-angle endpoints interchanged. Their intersection has base 12, base angles 30°, and area \(12\sqrt3\).

methods.label: Find the triangular overlap
methods.explanation:
Interpret partial overlap as positive common area without complete coincidence. Label the common hypotenuse \(AB\). The triangles must lie on the same side of \(AB\), and their \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) angles at its endpoints must be interchanged; otherwise they would coincide completely.

At each endpoint, the side making \(30^\circ\) with \(AB\) gives the tighter boundary next to the base. Thus the common region is triangle \(APB\), where these two sides meet, with
\[
\angle PAB=\angle PBA=30^\circ.
\]
These equal base angles make \(APB\) isosceles. Its altitude \(PM\) therefore bisects \(AB\), so \(AM=6\).

Write \(PM=h>0\). In right triangle \(AMP\), the side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse, so \(AP=2h\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
6^2+h^2=(2h)^2,
\qquad 3h^2=36,
\qquad h=2\sqrt3.
\]
Consequently, the common area is
\[
\frac12\cdot12\cdot2\sqrt3=\boxed{12\sqrt3},
\]
which is choice D.
